draft.title: Factors affecting respiration
card: The rate of cellular respiration is how fast a cell uses glucose and makes ATP. Temperature, glucose supply and oxygen supply all change it.
Temperature
respiration is controlled by enzymes. A rise in temperature speeds up the reactions until the optimum, and past it the enzymes denature and the rate drops sharply.
Glucose
more glucose gives the enzymes more substrate, so the rate rises. It levels off once the enzymes are working at their maximum rate.
Oxygen
oxygen is the final electron acceptor in the electron transport chain. With less oxygen the chain slows, so less ATP is made, and the cell relies more on anaerobic pathways.
draft.remember: Enzymes, glucose and oxygen set the rate: more helps until a limit is reached.

a.q: A student warms yeast in glucose solution from 10 °C to 35 °C and the rate of respiration rises. What is the best explanation?
opts: Enzyme reactions speed up as temperature rises
Glucose is made faster at higher temperature
Oxygen is no longer needed by the cell
More enzymes are made at higher temperature
a.why: Respiration depends on enzymes, and warmth makes enzyme reactions happen faster up to the optimum. The cell does not make more enzymes in the short term because of the heat, so that option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what controls each step of respiration.

b.q: Researchers raise the glucose concentration around muscle cells in a dish with plenty of oxygen. At first the rate of respiration rises, then it stops rising. What is the most likely reason?
opts: The enzymes are working at their maximum rate
The cells have run out of glucose to use
The extra glucose has denatured the enzymes
The electron transport chain no longer needs oxygen
b.why: Once all the enzymes are busy, extra glucose cannot speed things up, so the rate levels off. The cells have not run out of glucose, because the supply was raised, so that option is wrong.
b.clue: The glucose supply is high, so what else could limit the rate?

a.best: Enzyme reactions speed up as temperature rises

b.best: The enzymes are working at their maximum rate
